newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares rise in active cement trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares rise in active cement trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices rose on Thursday after active trade in the cement sector and the listing of new shares in a partially privatised spinning and weaving firm.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) overall index rose 1.00 to 324.08 points in high turnover of 122.00 million pounds ($35.80 million).
The CMAreport said the listing of a further 1.238 million shares in United Arab Spinning and Weaving/Unirab at 75.00 pounds a share accounted for almost 93 million pounds of the day's volume.
The Egyptian government said it would offer investors a minimum of 10 percent in the partially privatised firm for two days from January 8.
Three cement firms made the day's top 10 most active stocks.
Amriyah Cement topped the list, but it rose 3.44 pounds to close at 74 after trade worth more than 4 million pounds.

Helwan Portland Cement ended 0.70 pounds lower at 68.50 after trading in more than 2 million pounds and Suez Cement gained 1.30 pounds to close at 63.30 after shares worth almost 2 million pounds exchanged hands.

Housing firms, which led the way on Wednesday, slipped slightly. Medinet Nasr Housing and Development, which was Wednesday's most active share, lost 9.10 pounds to close at 415.00 with 2 million pounds turnover.
Heliopolis Housing and Development gained 9.00 pounds to close at 471.00 with turnover of more than 940,000 pounds.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 518.77 points from 514.95 on Wednesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms also rose to 219.45 from 219.37.
Of the 70 shares traded, 31 gained, 18 lost and 21 ended the day unchanged.
